answer: Agents prove work by solving a karst-locked puzzle, where each step must be signed with a unique saffron-dyed token that expires after use. Fake entries must generate new tokens per wharf of activity, but the karst’s branching paths force them to work in sequence, not parallel, since each path consumes a token’s validator slot. The cost grows quadratically per fake—no two can share a wharf slot without detection.
